request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

agent.result_text:
Three of the four tests pass. The fourth (scenario 3) fails only because the spec itself has an error I can't fix: it isn't allowed to be edited, and the only way around it would be faking the output.

**The numbering change** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/ClaimRepository.java`): when a claim is opened outside period numbering, the app now:
- works out the sheet's tree by following parents up to the top sheet, then collecting every sheet below it;
- locks all those sheets in id order, so two claims opened at once can't get the same number;
- gives the claim one more than the highest last number on any sheet of the tree, and records that as this sheet's last number.

Numbers already given don't change, and period numbers (`P1-1`, `X-1`) still count per sheet. No new stored data was needed: the existing per-sheet last number is enough.

**A second fix scenario 3 needed** (`src/main/frontend/features/people/people.slot.tsx`): the test adds "Ada" with terms 3 and contact ADA@X. The server refuses this because names must be unique across the tree. The form kept those values, so the next person, Cam, was saved with them. That made Cam's claim overdue too early, and the test expects Cam's terms and contact to be empty. Now, when the server refuses an add, the form clears terms and contact. The form already cleared contact when it refused a duplicate contact itself.

**The spec error:** lines 1073 and 1151 of `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` expect `sheet-parent` to show the literal text `__SHEET__-p`. It looks like a placeholder that was never filled in; every other line uses `` `${sheet}-p` ``. The app shows the real parent id. I ran a temporary copy of the spec with just that placeholder filled in, and scenario 3 passed all the way through. I deleted the copy afterwards. The spec needs those two lines fixed.

**If you run `bin/e2e` yourself:** in this shell `PORT=3002`, and port 3002 is already used by another sandbox's app that was running before I started. Ours then fails to start and every test fails at its first step. I left that process alone and ran the tests with `PORT=3017 bin/e2e`.
